newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Tingyi parent mulls Taiwan investment.
newsitem.headline: Tingyi parent mulls Taiwan investment.

text.p: Instant noodle maker Tingyi (Cayman Islands) Holdings Corp said on Monday its Taiwanese parent, Ting Hsin (Cayman Islands) Holding Corp, was mulling a T$10 billion investment in Taiwan.
Tingyi said in a statement that the Hong Kong-listed unit itself was not considering making such an investment in Taiwan.

"The board would like to clarify that the company does not have such an investment plan, and it is an investment plan of the company's parent, Ting Hsin (Cayman Island) Holding Corp," the statement said.

A Ting Hsin official said on Friday that the group was considering investing in Taiwan, and indicated Tingyi wanted to comply with a Taiwan government call for local enterprises to consider reinvesting in Taiwan rather than in mainland China.
Tingyi, a major player in the Chinese instant noodle market, said on Monday it wanted to clarify the sitation and added it remained committed to its food and beverage business in China.
Tingyi shares were unchanged at HK$1.90 on Monday.
